Settsmartly – Competitive Strategy & Differentiated Product Blueprint

Settsmartly

Your Household. Your Money. One Smart Platform.

Strategic product direction

My recommendation is to build Settsmartly around one very specific problem:

Managing money in a shared household is unnecessarily complicated. Settsmartly makes it organized, intelligent and transparent.

We are not building just another application where people enter expenses and divide them by four.

We are building a shared household financial management platform for Indian flatmates and working professionals, with an AI-powered voice assistant as its signature innovation.

The strategy will have five pillars:

  1. Household financial management.

  2. AI-powered voice expense entry.

  3. Smart recurring bill management.

  4. Intelligent settlements and payment reconciliation.

  5. Household financial intelligence.

The most important strategic decision is to make Settsmartly exceptionally useful for people living together, rather than trying to serve every possible expense-sharing use case from day one.

1. Our exact market positioning

Positioning statement

Not just expense splitting. Complete household financial management.

Settsmartly helps flatmates and working professionals manage shared household expenses, recurring bills, individual contributions and settlements through one intelligent platform.

Brand promise

Know where every rupee goes. Know who paid. Know what is pending. Manage everything together.

Who exactly are we building for?

Our initial ideal customer is:

  • A working professional aged approximately 21–35.

  • Living in a rented apartment with 2–5 flatmates.

  • Sharing rent, groceries, electricity, internet and maintenance.

  • Regularly using UPI.

  • Currently coordinating payments through WhatsApp, spreadsheets or manual calculations.

Our initial geographic market should be Bengaluru, followed by Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Mumbai and other major Indian cities.

The problem we want to own

Imagine five people living in one apartment.

Every month they need to manage:

Expense

Monthly amount

Rent

₹15,000

Groceries

₹5,000

Electricity

₹2,000

Internet

₹999

Water and maintenance

₹1,500

Household supplies

₹1,000

Total household spending is ₹25,499.

The problem isn't simply dividing ₹25,499 by five.

The real problems are:

  • Different people pay different bills.

  • Some expenses are shared by everyone, others only by selected members.

  • Someone moves out in the middle of the month.

  • Someone pays late.

  • Bills recur every month.

  • People forget transactions.

  • Nobody has a complete picture of household spending.

This entire workflow is our business opportunity.

2. Competitive landscape: Who are we really competing against?

I checked the current product positioning of several relevant competitors. There is an important finding that changes how we should build Settsmartly.

Fave UPI

Closest household competitor

Fave already targets flatmates, couples and families, with shared spending, UPI payments and a bill calendar.

fave+2

Established expense competitor

It offers group expenses, multiple split types, recurring expenses, debt simplification, receipt scanning and analytics.

Splitwise+2

It supports custom splits, receipt photos, payment requests, offline tracking and spending insights.

Shared expenses, splits and repayments+1

AI voice competitor

Its website advertises voice expense entry, receipt scanning, AI insights, recurring expenses and automatic debt simplification.

Split smarter. Settle faster.

The important strategic lesson

We cannot claim that voice entry, AI receipts, UPI or household bill tracking individually make us unique.

Fave already occupies much of the household/UPI positioning. Splitwise covers many expense-management capabilities. SplitEase already markets AI voice entry.

Our opportunity is to combine these capabilities into a more complete and specialized experience:

A voice-first household financial operating system with intelligent roommate lifecycle management.

That is a much stronger direction.

3. Our signature innovation: Settsmartly AI Voice Assistant

Primary product differentiator to develop

This should be the most recognizable feature of Settsmartly.

The idea is simple:

Users should be able to manage household expenses by speaking naturally instead of filling out forms.

Example 1: Normal expense entry

User says:

"I paid 2,500 rupees for groceries today. Split equally between all five flatmates."

The assistant extracts:

Illustrative interface. The assistant must never save an expense without user confirmation.

Example 2: Hinglish voice support

User says:

"Aaj electricity ka 1800 rupees bill pay kiya, sabke beech equally divide kar do."

The assistant should understand the mixed Hindi-English request and prepare the expense.

Example 3: Household expense

User says:

"Add 800 rupees for cleaning supplies, but exclude Aman because he moved out."

The system should:

  1. Identify the expense.

  2. Identify the amount.

  3. Identify the excluded member.

  4. Check the group's membership and expense-sharing rules.

  5. Prepare the split.

  6. Ask for confirmation.

Example 4: Ask questions about household finances

User asks:

"How much did we spend on groceries last month?"

The assistant should calculate the answer using actual recorded group expenses.

Other supported questions:

  • Who owes me the most?

  • What is our total monthly rent?

  • How much did I personally spend?

  • Which bills are still unpaid?

  • What are our upcoming payments?

  • How much did we spend this week?

Example 5: Voice-based corrections

User says:

"Change the electricity bill from 1,800 to 2,000."

The assistant prepares an edit, displays the before-and-after values and requests confirmation.

How the AI should work

User speaks

AI intent and entity extraction

Amount · Payer · Category · Members · Split

User reviews and approves

Expense saved

Critical safety rule: AI can interpret instructions, but the backend must calculate financial shares. AI should never independently decide or execute financial transactions.

A feature I particularly recommend: Roommate lifecycle management

This can become an excellent specialization for Settsmartly.

Imagine Aman moves out on the 15th of the month.

The app should help the household:

  • Record Aman's move-out date.

  • Calculate his eligible rent share based on the agreed policy.

  • Exclude him from future expenses after the effective date.

  • Calculate his pending balances.

  • Record refundable security deposits separately.

  • Invite a replacement flatmate.

  • Add the new member with the correct joining date.

  • Preserve the historical financial records.

For example:

Roommate transition example

Illustrative calculation

Assume ₹15,000 monthly rent, 30-day month and an agreed daily pro-rata policy.

₹7,500

Aman’s rent share for 15 days.

Monthly rent ₹15,000
Days occupied 15
Daily rent ₹500

Rent share ₹7,500

The actual allocation should follow the household's agreed rental arrangement, not automatically assume every bill is prorated.

This is more than expense splitting. It is household financial administration.

5. Complete MVP: What we should actually launch

I recommend a focused MVP rather than attempting to develop every feature immediately.

Our MVP should solve one complete problem: managing the finances of a shared apartment for an entire month.

Recommended MVP scope

Module 1 – Authentication and user profiles

  • Mobile OTP login.

  • Google login.

  • Profile creation.

  • Profile photo.

  • Mobile verification.

  • UPI ID management.

  • Account security and logout.

Module 2 – Household creation

  • Create a household.

  • Add a household name and address label.

  • Invite flatmates.

  • Set household administrator.

  • Assign membership dates.

  • Add household sharing rules.

  • Remove or deactivate members.

  • Maintain historical membership.

Module 3 – Expense management

  • Add an expense manually.

  • Add expenses through voice.

  • Add expenses using receipt images.

  • Select payer.

  • Select participating members.

  • Equal splitting.

  • Custom amount splitting.

  • Percentage splitting.

  • Shares-based splitting.

  • Edit and delete expenses with an audit trail.

Module 4 – AI voice assistant

This is our signature feature.

  • English voice input.

  • Hindi voice input.

  • Hinglish voice input.

  • Natural language expense creation.

  • Voice-based expense correction.

  • Ask questions about recorded expenses.

  • Voice-based bill categorization.

  • Clarification when information is missing.

  • Review and confirmation before saving.

For the first release, I would support voice expense creation and basic financial questions. More advanced conversational actions can come later.

Module 5 – Recurring bill management

  • Rent schedules.

  • Electricity reminders.

  • Water bills.

  • Internet bills.

  • Maintenance expenses.

  • Monthly subscriptions.

  • Upcoming bill calendar.

  • Overdue bill notifications.

  • Individual member contributions.

Module 6 – Settlement management

  • Member-wise outstanding balances.

  • Suggested settlement transactions.

  • UPI payment intent links.

  • Payment reference records.

  • Manual payment confirmation.

  • Pending payment status.

  • Settlement history.

  • Duplicate settlement protection.

Module 7 – Financial dashboard

  • Monthly household expenditure.

  • Individual contributions.

  • Category-wise spending.

  • Outstanding balances.

  • Upcoming bills.

  • Monthly comparisons.

  • Spending trends.

Module 8 – Notifications

  • New expense notifications.

  • Bill reminders.

  • Settlement reminders.

  • Member invitations.

  • Expense modifications.

  • Payment confirmation updates.

  • Monthly household summaries.

What should NOT be in our first release?

I would postpone:

  • Lending or credit products.

  • Holding customer money.

  • Automatic bank debits.

  • Full accounting software.

  • Complex investment features.

  • Merchant marketplace.

  • Advanced multi-currency travel management.

These would increase development complexity and distract us from the core customer problem.

6. The feature that could become our strongest competitive advantage

Signature experience

Just speak. Your household gets organized.

Imagine opening Settsmartly and saying:

"Our rent is 15,000 rupees. Add it as a monthly recurring expense and split equally between the five active flatmates."

Settsmartly prepares the bill, identifies the participants, calculates their shares and asks for confirmation.

dribbble.com

This should be the product experience people associate with Settsmartly.

How to make voice genuinely better

Simply converting speech into text is not enough. We need five capabilities:

Capability

Expected behaviour

Context awareness

Understand which household the user is referring to

Member recognition

Identify members by their names and nicknames

Mixed-language support

Understand Hindi-English combinations

Financial understanding

Understand amounts, percentages and dates

Conversation memory

Remember relevant context within a conversation

For example:

User: "Add 500 for groceries."

Assistant: "Should I add ₹500 to Bangalore Flat and split it equally among the five active members?"

User: "No, exclude Aman."

Assistant: "Understood. I'll prepare a ₹500 expense split among the other four members, ₹125 each."

User: "Confirm."

Assistant: Saves the expense.

We should only perform this final save after explicit authorization.

Important technical safeguards

  1. Calculate all balances on the trusted backend.

  2. Use transactional database operations for expense and settlement changes.

  3. Preserve historical membership and expense records.

  4. Require authorization before accessing household financial data.

  5. Do not treat an opened UPI application as proof of successful payment.

  6. Keep voice recordings and transcripts protected, with clear consent and retention controls.

  7. Require user confirmation for financial actions suggested by AI.

  8. Ensure that repeated API requests cannot accidentally create duplicate expenses.

10. Why now? The Indian market opportunity

India is a promising market for a UPI-connected shared-finance product.

According to Government of India figures based on NPCI data, UPI processed approximately 24,161.69 crore transactions in FY 2025–26, with transaction value of approximately ₹314 lakh crore. UPI accounted for around 85% of India's digital payment volume.

Press Information Bureau+1

This supports the idea that users are already comfortable with digital payments.

However, payment adoption does not automatically prove demand for another expense application. We need to validate whether flatmates actually want a dedicated household financial workspace and whether voice makes the experience meaningfully better.

Our initial market-entry strategy

Stage 1 – Bengaluru

Target IT professionals, shared apartments, PG residents and working professionals.

Initial launch market

Stage 2 – Major Indian cities

Expand to Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai and Mumbai after validating retention.

Stage 3 – Broader household market

Expand into couples, families, student accommodation and other shared financial arrangements.

12. What will make our competitive advantage defensible?

This is particularly important if we want to raise investment.

Features alone are not a long-term moat. Competitors can copy features.

We need to develop advantages that improve as more households use Settsmartly.

I would focus on four potential advantages.

1. Household financial history

Over time, Settsmartly can develop a detailed, user-authorized history of each household's expenses, recurring bills, membership changes and settlement records.

This makes the application more useful over time.

2. Household-specific AI context

The assistant can understand:

  • Who lives in the household.

  • Who participates in each recurring expense.

  • What the usual rent arrangement is.

  • Which bills are shared.

  • Which members have moved out.

  • How household spending changes over time.

3. Household workflow specialization

Instead of just storing transactions, Settsmartly manages the lifecycle of shared living, including joining, leaving, recurring obligations and final settlements.

4. Distribution through existing groups

Every household invitation can introduce additional users. If the product becomes useful to the entire household, it can create a natural network effect.

These are potential competitive advantages, not proven moats. They become meaningful only if we achieve strong adoption, retention and reliable data quality.

13. First 90-day execution plan

I would approach development and validation in four stages.

  1. Days 1–15: Customer validation

    • Interview 30–50 flatmates in Bengaluru.

    • Understand their current expense-management process.

    • Identify their biggest monthly financial problems.

    • Test whether people actually want voice-based expense entry.

    • Validate the willingness to pay for household management.

  2. Days 16–35: Core product development

    • OTP authentication.

    • Household creation.

    • Member invitations.

    • Expense creation.

    • Expense splitting.

    • Balance calculations.

    • Basic UPI payment handoff.

  3. Days 36–60: Differentiated features

    • Voice expense assistant.

    • Hindi and Hinglish support.

    • Recurring bill management.

    • Household calendar.

    • Membership dates.

    • Roommate move-in/move-out calculations.

  4. Days 61–90: Closed beta

    • Launch with 30–50 households.

    • Measure actual weekly usage.

    • Monitor voice recognition accuracy.

    • Measure expense completion rates.

    • Collect feedback.

    • Improve the experience before public launch.

14. Investor-ready unique value proposition

This is how I would describe Settsmartly in a pitch deck.

Settsmartly

The AI-powered financial operating system for shared living.

Settsmartly is building an India-first household financial management platform that helps flatmates and working professionals organize shared expenses, recurring bills, member contributions and settlements.

Unlike traditional expense trackers that primarily focus on recording and splitting transactions, Settsmartly aims to manage the complete household financial workflow through an intelligent voice-first assistant.

Our vision: Make managing shared money as easy as having a conversation.

Core value proposition

  • Speak naturally to record expenses.

  • Manage all household bills in one place.

  • Automatically calculate individual contributions.

  • Understand outstanding balances.

  • Manage changing household memberships.

  • Get intelligent financial insights.

15. Your 30-second investor pitch

Writing

Settsmartly is building an AI-powered household financial management platform for India's growing population of flatmates and working professionals.

Today, people sharing apartments manage rent, groceries, electricity, internet and other household expenses through fragmented tools, WhatsApp messages and manual calculations.

Existing expense-sharing applications help people divide bills, but we believe there is an opportunity to go further.

Settsmartly brings shared expenses, recurring household bills, member contributions and payment settlements into one intelligent platform.

Our signature innovation is an AI-powered voice assistant that allows users to manage expenses naturally in English, Hindi and Hinglish, without manually filling out forms.

We are starting with shared apartments and working professionals in Bengaluru, with the long-term vision of becoming the financial operating system for shared living across India.

17. Final strategic recommendation

My recommended company direction

I would build Settsmartly with this hierarchy:

Settsmartly

Complete household financial management.

Core product

Expense tracking, splitting, household management and settlements.

Signature innovation

18. What should we finalize next?

I recommend turning this strategy into a professional, developer-ready Product Requirements Document (PRD), so the design and development work has one clear source of truth.

The PRD should include:

  • Every application module.

  • Every screen and screen interaction.

  • Voice assistant conversation flows.

  • AI prompts and structured output requirements.

  • Expense calculation rules.

  • Database schema and relationships.

  • API endpoints.

  • User permissions.

  • Payment and settlement logic.

  • Security requirements.

  • Admin dashboard.

  • Testing scenarios.

  • Development milestones.

The first thing I would prototype is the AI assistant: a user speaks one sentence, the app correctly understands the household context, prepares an expense and gets confirmation before saving.

That experience should be the heart of Settsmartly.
